result.title: AnomalyJev: Towards Evaluating Image Anomaly Explanations via Claim-Level Verification
result.summary: Recent multimodal LLM (MLLM)-based anomaly detection (AD) methods can generate textual explanations that help interpret their predictions. However, reliably and efficiently evaluating these explanations remains challenging. While LLM judges can assess explanations through structured rubrics, they often require substantial token generation, making evaluation costly and difficult to scale. We instead propose to anchor evaluation in the available ground truth by extracting verifiable claims from each explanation and verifying them against the corresponding annotations. We instantiate this idea as AnomalyJev, a lightweight framework that extracts verifiable claims from contextualised representations using ground-truth-defined queries and pointer based heads, without token generation. The claims are then verified against the ground truth to score faithfulness and completeness. For evaluation, we construct a human-annotated set of 640 explanations with over 1,600 expert ratings across in-domain and cross-dataset settings. Despite its compact design, AnomalyJev achieves stronger agreement with human annotators than most open MLLM judges and approaches that of flagship MLLM judges, at a fraction of their runtime and resources.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 AnomalyJev，用真值定义的查询与 pointer head 从上下文表示中直接抽取可核验的 claim，再对照标注验证以评分 MLLM 异常检测解释的忠实性与完整性，并构建了含 640 条人工评分的评测集。
AI.relevance_reason: 无 token 生成的 claim 抽取与验证思路，或可供核查能否用于廉价地检验 latent/视觉推理状态中所含证据与结论是否可核验、忠实，但任务场景为异常检测解释评测，迁移性待判断。
